messages:
sophie: Heads up — scheduled cutover in ~2h for release/3.7.0. I see deploy-bot flagged a compliance issue during staging SBOM/vuln checks. Need quick evidence so we can decide: short hold + sign/patch, or rollback to 3.6.9. Please post artifacts/logs here.

alan: quick status — build & unit tests green. canary passed. SBOM job ran but signature step errored out: `cosign: signing process failed: no key available`

maria: deploy-bot output pasted below. i kicked off sbom-sign job again (job id: sbom-sign-4680). if the signer picks up the key it should succeed in ~2–3m.

deploy-bot: scan: vuln-scan-staging/4680012310 completed
Found: 1 medium (libpng 1.6.37) — exploitability low
SBOM: generated but unsigned (cosign exit code 2)
Artifacts: gcr.io/redwood/release/3.7.0-canary@sha256:abcd1234

leo: tagging in — from security POV: medium vuln acceptable for canary if we have mitigations and a signed SBOM attached to the release within the change window. We need either: (A) signed SBOM + mitigation note (why vuln acceptable + timeline), or (B) rollback to 3.6.9. no silent roll-forwards.

nate: what's our rollback criteria? if signer doesn't succeed, are we comfortable doing a quick revert to the last pinned image? that is, stop rollout and point traffic back to 3.6.9. who owns the rollback?

alan: rollback playbook is `releases/rollback-quick` — ops runbooks, last author @alan. takes ~7m to redirect frontends and revert canary. i can own if needed.

maria: sbom-sign job now shows `cosign: signed successfully` — uploading attestation now. artifact now has `cosign.sig` on bucket.

deploy-bot: attestation upload: success (s3://redwood-artifacts/attestations/3.7.0-canary/cosign.sig)
Vuln scan: 1 medium (libpng) — CVE-2019-12345 — no public exploit in the wild; score 5.3

leo: ok — need a short mitigation note to pair with the attestation. please include: why vuln accepted, compensating control (image scanned at runtime w/ exploit detection), follow-up patch timeline (target next minor within 30 days).

sophie: can someone paste the signed sbom hash + link and a one-liner mitigation note? ops needs to confirm before cutover. if we get both within 45m we proceed; otherwise we revert. timebox set.

nate: recommended mitigation note: `Evaluated libpng CVE-2019-12345: low exploitability for our workload; runtime detection via image-monitor / IDS; patch scheduled for 3.7.1 within 21 days.`

alan: SBOM hash: `sha256:9f8e7d6a5b4c3d2e1f0a1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef1234567890ab`
Signed attestation: https://artifacts.internal.redwood/sbom/3.7.0-canary/cosign.sig

maria: pushing mitigation note into release notes draft and adding a PROV comment referencing the attestation.

leo: i accept this as evidence. security sign-off given for cutover in EU canary region only — full global rollover requires an ITP (issue tracked) but allowed under canary policy.

deploy-bot: action: canary rollout -> EU region only (50% traffic), planned cutover 4680015600.

sophie: thanks. decision: proceed with EU canary cutover now that signed SBOM + mitigation note exist. we will hold global rollout until monitoring shows no anomalous signals for 2 hours or until 3.7.1 is ready, whichever comes first. if any new blocker appears we will trigger rollback to 3.6.9 (alan owner).

maria: noted and updated release notes + changelog entry.

nate: adding rollback watch on PagerDuty (schedule: releases-oncall).

leo: logging final acceptance in the compliance tracker (ticket #SEC-5932).

sophie: closing loop — will follow up with a short postmortem note if we need to revert. :thumbsup:
